title: Real-world validation of multi-exception scoping against authoritative GDPR Art 9 scenarios, no tuning
goal: Re-validate EXP-085's OR-combination mechanism (split_exceptions/check_exceptions, unchanged) against real-world scenarios fetched from authoritative sources -- the UK ICO's own published worked examples and a real GDPR enforcement decision -- phrased as those sources actually state them, with no rewording toward the GDPR clause's own vocabulary and no iteration against the model's score, directly answering the objection that EXP-085's own validation sentences were tuned to pass rather than drawn from real evidence.
method: Same rule/fact fixture as EXP-085 (lab.exp_085_multi_exception_scoping.run.RULE_TEXT/FACT_TEXT, imported unchanged), run through the same unmodified forward_chain/check_exceptions. Four context texts replace EXP-085's hand-tuned sentences: three ICO worked examples (one per exception, each expected to measure as 'holds') and one real AEPD enforcement decision describing an actual Article 9 violation on an unrelated fact pattern (expected to measure as 'unknown', not 'not_holds', since it never specifically addresses any of the three listed exceptions). Each case's measured status is compared to its expected real-world conclusion and reported, match or not, with no retry.
results_prose: 3/4 cases' measured status matched the real-world expected conclusion, with no wording retried or tuned after seeing a score. consent_ico_gym: expected='holds', measured='holds' (matches_expected=True) -- per-exception: [holds(e=0.7943,c=0.0039), unknown(e=0.0806,c=0.0287), unknown(e=0.0081,c=0.0056)] | vital_interests_ico_unconscious: expected='holds', measured='holds' (matches_expected=True) -- per-exception: [not_holds(e=0.0014,c=0.9702), holds(e=0.9371,c=0.0041), unknown(e=0.0694,c=0.0085)] | legal_claims_ico_tribunal: expected='holds', measured='unknown' (matches_expected=False) -- per-exception: [unknown(e=0.0042,c=0.0047), unknown(e=0.2637,c=0.0154), unknown(e=0.691,c=0.0083)] | violation_aepd_eurocollege: expected='unknown', measured='unknown' (matches_expected=True) -- per-exception: [unknown(e=0.0054,c=0.0076), unknown(e=0.058,c=0.013), unknown(e=0.0107,c=0.0086)]
conclusion: On real worked examples fetched from the UK ICO's own published guidance and a real AEPD enforcement decision -- never reworded to mirror GDPR Art 9's own clause phrasing, never tuned against the model's score -- 3/4 cases matched the expected real-world conclusion. At least one real-world scenario did not match the expected conclusion -- see metrics.per_exception for the exact entailment/contradiction scores measured. This is the honest finding EXP-085's hand-tuned validation could not surface: check_exception's entailment gate may not generalize past text engineered to closely mirror the exception clause's own wording, which is exactly the brittleness EXP-085's own follow-ups already flagged as a real risk on natural (not hand-tuned) context text.
scale_down: Four real scenarios (three ICO worked examples plus one enforcement decision), not a broad corpus of case law -- a real validation of the mechanism's entailment gate against authoritative, unmodified source language, not a comprehensive legal benchmark. Each ICO scenario is restated as a short declarative summary close to the source's own wording rather than quoted at full length -- reproducing the full guidance page verbatim was neither necessary nor appropriate to copy at length.
follow_ups: If any case's measured status did not match its expected real-world conclusion (see metrics), the real next step is NOT to reword that case's context text to force a match -- that would repeat exactly the tuning this exploration exists to avoid. It is either accepting check_exception's current entailment gate as genuinely limited to lexically-close evidence, or testing whether a different NLI checkpoint / a sentence-splitting preprocessing step (EXP-083's own named follow-up) closes the gap -- a separate, measured exploration either way.

Only one real-world sentence was tested per exception; a single sentence is also EXP-083's and EXP-085's own known scale-down (check_exception reads one premise at a time) -- a longer real passage with the relevant evidence buried among unrelated sentences was not tested here either.
models_used: MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli (per-exception entailment via the existing, unmodified check_exception/check_exceptions). No generative model. No new dependency.
